target_customer: Satellite operators, government agencies and research organizations that need to move payloads between orbits
problem: Rideshare rockets drop small satellites into a fixed orbit, so operators cannot reach their target orbit without an in-space transfer vehicle.
business_model: Per-mission in-space transportation and hosted payload services, later also satellite bus and service module sales
product_category: Orbital transfer vehicle, water plasma propulsion

founders.name: Mikhail Kokorich
previous_startups: Earlier YC company (the YC page calls him a 2 time YC founder)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a physicist and self taught engineer, listed under former founders.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build a novel water plasma thruster and a free flying orbital vehicle, then obtain launch and licensing approval. Hardware, propulsion and regulatory risk all stacked.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary propulsion and launch licensing were hard to copy, but the model depended on a few launch providers and later flight failures weakened the position.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it by the batch. Later rivals such as Exotrail, D-Orbit and Impulse Space entered the same niche, per 2026 roundups.

market_need_then: Smallsat rideshare launches were growing and operators could not choose orbits. The 2019 Series A coverage cites two shuttle vehicles under development. No dated demand figure was found.

identity.logo: Stacked white wordmark on the company site

branding.community_and_virality: Brand press was about the SEC fraud case and SPAC trouble, not the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Known mainly through SPAC coverage and the SEC action over misleading test claims. No evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Momentus raised a seed and a 2019 Series A, then went public by SPAC in 2021 at a valuation cut roughly in half from the first deal terms. The SEC said it misled investors about a successfully tested technology and it paid 7 million dollars to settle. Launch delays and shrinking cash led to layoffs of about a fifth of staff and a later pivot toward selling the tug as a service module.
notes: No competitor source dated near mid 2018 was found, so the list is empty. Later SPAC financing totals vary from 39.5M to 152.9M across aggregators and are unverified. SPAC close date not confirmed in sources read. Status is Public per YC. A search did not find a current 2026 final outcome.
